# bd-apvhh — how many findings each inventory rule OWNS.
#
# `classify_finding` takes the FIRST rule whose fragment appears in a finding's
# +/-4 context window, so a rule's blast radius is not visible from its text. A
# fragment that owns 3 sites today and 30 next month has silently become a
# different rule, and nothing said so.
#
# This ledger makes that visible. The gate fails in BOTH directions:
#   - a rule owning MORE than its declared count absorbed sites nobody reviewed;
#   - a rule owning FEWER is stale and the number must come down.
# One arm without the other is how a ledger decays into decoration.
#
# A count of 0 is a rule that classifies NOTHING. Those are dead weight, not
# coverage -- but "owns zero" is TWO defects and this line originally named only
# the first (bd-epvc1, measured 2026-09-17: 33 of 331 rules own zero):
#   - SHADOWED (6): the fragment really does match findings and an EARLIER rule
#     wins them. Check whether the absorber's reason covers what it absorbed.
#   - DEAD FRAGMENT (27): the fragment matches no finding at all, shadowed or
#     not. Eight of those are must_fix rules, each naming a follow-up bead while
#     watching nothing, which is the actionable half.
#
# WHAT A GREEN HERE DOES NOT MEAN. Both arms fire when a count MOVES. Neither
# can fire on shadowing that ALREADY EXISTED when these numbers were recorded,
# because they were recorded from current behaviour -- an absorbing rule's count
# was written down with the absorption already inside it. So this ledger
# certifies today's shadowing as correct and guards only tomorrow's. It is a
# ratchet pinned to the day it was taken. That is a bound on the green, not a
# reason to distrust the arms; the pre-existing shadowing is bd-epvc1's job.
#
# Recorded 2026-09-17 against the detector at that commit. Regenerate by
# reading the gate, never by hand-adjusting a number to make it pass.
#
# Format: <count>\t<rule id>

# bd-apvhh 2026-09-17: the first FUNCTION-SCOPED group rules. The count is
# multiplicity within one function, not a per-occurrence identity -- nine
# optional projection fields in from_ledger(), two of which are the identical
# line. A tenth appearing in that function FAILS this ledger, which is the
# property per-site keying was meant to buy and is why the check must stay
# two-directional.

# bd-apvhh burn-down tranche 5: the first file whose findings sit alongside
# EXISTING rules. From here first-match-wins is the dominant effect, so these
# four were appended at the END of INVENTORY_RULES rather than inserted near the
# front: at the end a new rule can only pick up findings no earlier rule matches,
# which makes "I did not steal anyone's count" structural instead of a promise.
#
# Verified with a per-rule delta across ALL 367 pre-existing rules, not just the
# four added: none moved. That zero was itself proved by temporarily inserting a
# rule at the FRONT with an existing rule's own fragment -- the check reported
# NSF-VERIFY-LEDGER-CODES-ABSENT going 1 -> 0, and the probe was removed. Worth
# recording why the proof mattered: during it the UNCLASSIFIED TOTAL did not
# move at all, 106 -> 106, so a totals comparison would have shown nothing while
# a rule was being silently re-aimed.

1	NSF-VERIFY-LEDGER-CLOSED-REMEDIATION-REFS
1	NSF-VERIFY-LEDGER-ERROR-CODES-FROM
